headline: Counter-Strike runs at 60 FPS on PSP with custom Rust 3D engine
summary: A modder created a Counter-Strike clone for PSP, running at 60 FPS with a custom 3D engine.
details: A developer, Yifeng Wang, successfully ported a Counter-Strike clone to the original Sony PSP, achieving 60 FPS gameplay at the device's native 480x272 resolution.
Wang created a custom Rust-based 3D engine called Pocket3D and a JavaScript engine called PocketJS for the game rules and UI.
The game runs on the PSP and PS Vita, with the full set of eight original Counter-Strike maps already tested.
The project is open-source, with a clean-room implemented FPS engine and a mod API.
caption:
Can Counter-Strike run on a 22-year-old PSP at 60 FPS?

A developer, Yifeng Wang, successfully ported a Counter-Strike clone to the original Sony PSP, achieving 60 FPS gameplay at the device's native 480x272 resolution.

Wang created a custom Rust-based 3D engine called Pocket3D and a JavaScript engine called PocketJS for the game rules and UI.

The game runs on the PSP and PS Vita, with the full set of eight original Counter-Strike maps already tested.

The project is open-source, with a clean-room implemented FPS engine and a mod API.

headline_marked: Researchers create [[programmable thermal device]] that steers heat
headline: Researchers create programmable thermal device that steers heat
summary: New device can control heat radiation and remember its state without power
details: Researchers from Osaka Metropolitan University have developed a programmable thermal device that can control where heat is radiated while remembering its configuration even after power is removed.
The device combines a magneto-optical material with a phase-change material to independently control how a surface absorbs and emits infrared radiation.
This breakthrough could eventually aid AI chip cooling and silicon photonics.
caption:
Can a material steer heat and remember its state without power?

Researchers from Osaka Metropolitan University have developed a programmable thermal device that can control where heat is radiated while remembering its configuration even after power is removed.

The device combines a magneto-optical material with a phase-change material to independently control how a surface absorbs and emits infrared radiation.

This breakthrough could eventually aid AI chip cooling and silicon photonics.
